safi-cedvel:54-59.t:
* I'rab:
(و) a conjunction (إلى ربّكم) attached to (أنيبوا); (له) attached to (أسلموا); (من قبل) attached to the two verbs (أنيبوا وأسلموا); (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative; (ثمّ) a conjunction; and (الواو) in (تنصرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتيكم ... ) is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أنيبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا تقنطوا «[Note: in the previous verse (53).]».
The clause «أسلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا تقنطوا.
The clause «يأتيكم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «لا تنصرون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), that is: "so when it comes to you you will be punished, then you will not be helped."
(55) (و) a conjunction; (ما) a relative noun in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi; the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (أنزل) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, "he", which is the ʿāʾid (the returning pronoun); (إليكم) attached to (أنزل); (من ربّكم) attached to (أنزل); (من قبل ... العذاب) as the first one, and the preposition is attached to (اتّبعوا); (بغتة) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it meets it in meaning «[Note: or it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "taking by surprise".]»; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لا) negative.
The clause «اتّبعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أسلموا.
The clause «أنزل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يأتيكم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «أنتم لا تشعرون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
The clause «لا تشعرون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
(56) (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative; (يا) a particle of vocative and lamentation; (حسرتا) the one addressed, one for whom lamentation is made, a muḍāf, accusative, its accusative marker being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the alif, which is converted from the (ياء), and that (ياء) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, attached to (حسرتا), its ʿāʾid being omitted.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقول) is in the position of an accusative, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with an omitted muḍāf; its governing word is أنيبوا.. «[Note: or its governing word is implied, i.e. "we warned you ..."]», that is: "for fear that a soul should say ..."
The interpreted maṣdar (ما فرّطت ... ) is in the position of a genitive after (على), attached to (حسرتا).
(في جنب) attached to (فرّطت); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (إن) the lightened form of the heavy (inna), and it is necessarily inoperative (muhmala); (اللام) the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa); (من الساخرين) attached to the khabar of كنت.
The clause «تقول نفس ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «يا حسرتا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «فرّطت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «كنت لمن الساخرين» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
(57) (أو) a conjunction; (تقول) an imperfect verb in the accusative, conjoined to the preceding (تقول); (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of (لو) .. (من المتّقين) attached to an omitted khabar of كنت.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله هداني) is in the position of a nominative, the fāʿil of an omitted verb whose implied form is ثبت, that is: (لو) "my guidance had been established, I would have been ..."
The clause «تقول.... (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تقول نفس (the first).
The clause «لو (ثبتت) هدايتي....» is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
The clause «هداني ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «كنت من المتّقين» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
(58) (أو تقول) like the preceding; (حين) an adverb of time in the accusative, attached to (تقول); (لو) a particle of wishing; (لي) attached to an omitted khabar of (أنّ); (كرّة) the ism of أنّ, accusative; (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation; (أكون) an incomplete imperfect verb, put in the accusative by an implied أن after the (الفاء), and its ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I); (من المحسنين) attached to the khabar of أكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون..) is conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the wish that came before, that is: "would that there were a return for me, so that my being one of those who do good ..." «[Note: It is permissible for the interpreted maṣdar to be conjoined to (كرّة) without regard to causation in the fāʾ. The difference between the two cases is that the conjunction above makes the "being" consequent upon the wish, whereas, without regard to causation, the "being" is itself wished for, as is the case with the word كرّة.]».
The clause «تقول....» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تقول (the second).
The clause «ترى....» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لي كرة) is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
(59) (بلى) a particle of response, affirming the negated question; (قد) a particle of certainty (taḥqīq); (الفاء) a conjunction; (بها) attached to (كذّبت); (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (من الكافرين) attached to the khabar of كنت.
The clause «قد جاءتك آياتي ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech of an implied saying.
The clause «كذّبت ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause جاءتك آياتي.
The clause «استكبرت» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause كذّبت.
The clause «كنت من الكافرين» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause كذّبت..

* Morphology:
(الساخرين), plural of الساخر, an active participle from the triliteral verb سخر, of the pattern فرح, on the wazn فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Clarification (al-īḍāḥ): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَأَنِيبُوا إِلى رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ» .
It is conjoined to لا تقنطوا, to complete the clarification, as if it were said: "Do not despair of the mercy of Allah the Exalted, thinking that He will not accept your repentance, but turn to Him, the Exalted, and be sincere to Him, the Mighty and Majestic."
2- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, the Exalted, «أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ» .
The word «نفس» is made indefinite because what is meant by it is some of the souls, namely the soul of the disbeliever; it is also possible that a soul distinguished from the other souls is meant, either by stubbornness in disbelief that is severe or by a great punishment; and it is possible that multiplicity is meant, as al-Aʿshā said:
وربّ بقيع لو هتفت بجوّه ... أتاني كريم ينفض الرّأس مغضبا
(Many a level plain: had I called out in its midst, a noble man would have come to me, shaking his head in anger.)
He means droves of noble men who would help him, not one noble man. Its like is: "many a land I have crossed, many a hero I have faced", meaning many lands and heroes.
3- Metonymy (al-kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, «عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ» .
The original sense of الجنب is the bodily limb, then it is borrowed for the side and direction adjoining it, following their habit of borrowing the other limbs for that, such as "right" and "left"; and what is meant here is the direction, figuratively.
Neglect with regard to the direction of obedience is a metonymy for neglect of obedience itself, because whoever has lost a direction has all the more lost what is in it, the most eloquent way since it proceeds by demonstrative proof. Similar to that is the saying of Ziyād al-Aʿjam:
إن السماحة والمروءة والندى ... في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج
(Generosity, manliness and bounty are in a dome pitched over Ibn al-Ḥashraj.)
He means that he is singled out for these qualities, which are not found in anyone else; there is no tent there, and nothing was pitched at all.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أنزل); (الفاء) a conjunction; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of (ينابيع) [Note: it is either a second direct object, by implying in (سلكه) the meaning of "made it", or it is accusative as an adverbial if it means the spring-source and not the gushing water.]; (به) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يخرج), and the (ب) is causal; (ألوانه) agent of the active participle (مختلفا); (ثمّ) a conjunction in all three places, and likewise (الفاء); (في ذلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted element, the predicate of inna; (اللام) the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), for emphasis; (ذكرى) the noun of inna, accusative; (لأولي) attached to the verbal noun (ذكرى).
Clause: «لم تر ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «أنزل ... » is in the position of nominative, predicate of anna.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن الله أنزل..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of (ترى).
And the clause: «سلكه ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (أنزل).
And the clause: «يخرج ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (سلكه).
And the clause: «يهيج ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (يخرج) [Note: the conjunction is permissible despite the difference in predication, because the withering comes about by the power and will of Allah.] And the clause: «تراه مصفّرا» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (يهيج) [Note: that is, "so it turns yellow", i.e. Allah makes it yellow.] And the clause: «يجعله ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (يهيج).
And the clause: «إنّ في ذلك لذكرى ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istinʾāf bayānī).

* Morphology:
(حطاما): a noun meaning crumbled fragments, on the pattern فعال with ḍamma on the first letter, from the triliteral حطم, in the pattern of فرح, meaning "it shattered", and in the pattern of ضرب meaning "he broke".

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī); (الفاء) a conjunction; (من) a conditional noun governing the jussive, mubtadaʾ [Note: or a relative noun.. see verse (19) of this sūra, for the derivation of the i'rab is similar.]; (للإسلام) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb (شرح); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (على نور) attached to the predicate of the mubtadaʾ (هو); (من ربّه) attached to an adjective of (نور); (الفاء) resumptive; (ويل) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: for it indicates a supplication.]; (للقاسية) attached to the predicate of the mubtadaʾ (ويل); (قلوبهم) agent of the active participle (القاسية); (من ذكر) attached to (القاسية), and the preposition is causal; (في ضلال) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
Clause: «من شرح ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumptive clause of justification, namely: "Is he who submitted like the one who...? So he whose breast Allah has expanded..".
And the clause: «شرح ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: or it has no position if (من) is a relative noun, with the khabar of the mubtadaʾ omitted, its implied form being "like him whose heart has been sealed".].
And the clause: «هو على نور ... » is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the (فاء) [Note: it is possible that the clause is conjoined by the (فاء) to the ṣila clause.].
And the clause: «ويل للقاسية ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «أولئك في ضلال ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption, or a clause of justification.

* Benefits:
- The occurrence of (من) in the sense of (عن):
In the verse before us (من) occurs in the sense of "from/away from" (ʿan), in the words of the Exalted «فَوَيْلٌ لِلْقاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ», i.e. «عن ذكر الله», and in His words «يا وَيْلَنا قَدْ كُنَّا فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا», i.e. «عن هذا». It is also said: in this verse it is for the beginning of the range, to convey that what follows of punishment is more severe, as if this speaker links its meaning with (ويل), like the words of the Exalted «فَوَيْلٌ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النَّارِ»; but it is not sound that this be a technical attachment, because of the separation by the predicate. It is also said: in both it is for the beginning of the range, or in the first it is for causation, i.e. "because of the remembrance of Allah", for when He is mentioned their hearts harden.
Ibn Mālik claimed that (من) in a phrase such as (زيد أفضل من عمرو) is for transgression (mujāwaza), as if it were said: "Zayd surpassed ʿAmr in excellence". He said: this is better than the statement of Sībawayh and others that it is for the beginning of elevation in a phrase like (أفضل منه), and the beginning of lowness in a phrase like (شر منه), since (إلى) never follows it. It may be said: and if it were for transgression, it would be correct for (عن) to take its place.
Furthermore, the verse shows the active participle used in the sense of the resembling adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), in the words of the Exalted «فَوَيْلٌ لِلْقاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ». (قاسية) is an active participle, but it is a resembling adjective, because it indicates a fixed attribute in them, and this attribute took an agent, namely (قلوبهم). The rule says: when an active or passive participle occurs and indicates fixed attributes, they are considered a (resembling adjective), such as:
(هذا رجل معتدل القامة) ("this is a man of balanced stature") and (عليّ محمود السيرة) ("ʿAlī is of praiseworthy conduct").

safi-cedvel:23-23.t:
* I'rab:
(كتابا) badal from (أحسن); (مثاني) a second adjective of (كتاب), accusative; (منه) attached to (تقشعرّ); (إلى ذكر) attached to (تلين), by implying the meaning of "find rest" (تطمئنّ); (به) attached to (يهدي); (الواو) a conjunction; (من) a conditional noun governing the jussive, in the position of accusative, a fronted direct object whose operator is (يضلل); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (ما) negative, inoperative; (له) attached to a fronted predicate; (هاد) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ, the genitive marker being the implied kasra, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).
Clause: «الله نزّل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «نزّل ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
And the clause: «تقشعرّ منه جلود ... » is in the position of accusative, a third adjective of (كتابا) [Note: it may be a ḥāl from (كتابا) because it is qualified.].
And the clause: «يخشون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «تلين جلودهم ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause (تقشعرّ) [Note: or it has no position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.].
And the clause: «ذلك هدى الله ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يهدي ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from (هدى), the operator in it being the demonstrative (ذلك).
And the clause: «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من), the returning pronoun being omitted.
And the clause: «من يضلل الله ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (ذلك هدى).
And the clause: «ما له من هاد» is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the (فاء).

* Rhetoric:
1- Describing the singular with the plural: in the words of the Exalted «مَثانِيَ»:
Because the book is a whole with details, and the details of a thing are its whole and nothing else. Do you not say: the Qur'an is sevenths and fifths, sūras and verses; and likewise you say: stories, rulings and repeated exhortations; and its like is your saying: the human being is bones, veins and nerves.
2- The benefit of repetition: its benefit is the doubling (tathniya). Repetition is the fixing of speech in the mind, for souls are most averse to the discourse of exhortation, so unless it is repeated to them, again and again, it does not take root in them and does not do its work. Hence it was the custom of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to repeat to them what he exhorted and advised, three times and seven times, in order to plant it in their hearts and implant it in their breasts.
3- Vivid embodiment: in the words of the Exalted «تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ».
In this part of the verse are wonderful rhetorical points, the most important being vivid embodiment, for He, glory be to Him, wished to embody the extremity of their awe, so He presented an image in the dry skin and an image of standing hair. Do we not say: "the hair of his head stood up from fear"? The skins are mentioned alone first, and joined with the hearts second, because the awe whose seat is the hearts necessarily entails mention of the hearts; as if it were said: their skins shiver and their hearts are in awe at the first stage, and when they remember Allah and remember His mercy and its vastness, they exchange awe for hope in their hearts, and shivering for softness in their skins.
It is also said: the meaning is that since the Qur'an is at the utmost of eloquence and rhetorical force, whenever they saw their incapacity to rival it, their skins shivered from it in veneration of it and amazement at its beauty and eloquence; then their skins and hearts soften at the remembrance of Allah.

safi-cedvel:68-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (في الصور) deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil). (الفاء) conjunction in both places. (في السموات) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila (relative clause) of the first (من); likewise (في الأرض) is the ṣila of the second (من). (إلّا) for exception. (من) relative noun in the position of the accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). (ثمّ) conjunction. (فيه) deputy agent. (أخرى) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the verbal noun, and so it is its adjective «[Note: It is permissible for (أخرى) to be the deputy agent, the preposition and its noun being attached to (نفخ).]». (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya) ...
Clause: «نفخ في الصور..» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «صعق من....» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نفخ في الصور ...
And the clause: «شاء الله» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «نفخ فيه ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause صعق من ...
And the clause: «إذا هم قيام ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause نفخ فيه ...
And the clause: «ينظرون ... » in the position of the nominative, a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم «[Note: or in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قيام.]».
(69) (الواو) conjunction in the five places. (بنور) attached to (أشرقت). (بالنبيّين) deputy agent. (بينهم) adverbial accusative attached to (قضي). (بالحقّ) deputy agent. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (لا) negation.
And the clause: «أشرقت الأرض ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause هم قيام «[Note: It is permissible to cut it off as resumptive.]».
And the clause: «وضع الكتاب ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أشرقت.
And the clause: «جيء بالنبيّين ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أشرقت.
And the clause: «قضي.. بالحقّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أشرقت.
And the clause: «هم لا يظلمون» in the position of the accusative; ḥāl.
And the clause: «لا يظلمون» in the position of the nominative; khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
(70) (الواو) conjunction. (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun in the position of the accusative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of what it did", the returning pronoun being omitted.]». (الواو) the second, resumptive, or circumstantial. (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. "what they do".]».
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما عملت) is in the position of the accusative, a direct object, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of its doing".
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما يفعلون ... ) is in the position of the genitive by (الباء), attached to أعلم.
And the clause: «وفّيت كلّ نفس ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause قضي.
And the clause: «عملت ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the clause: «هو أعلم ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive «[Note: or it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.]».
And the clause: «يفعلون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the second particle-relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(69) جيء: the alif was restored to its origin to suit the passive; then its fāʾ was given a kasra because its ʿayn is originally kasra-vowelled; then the yāʾ was made sākin because the kasra on it is heavy.

* Rhetoric:
Metaphor (istiʿāra): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَأَشْرَقَتِ الْأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّها».
Allah the Mighty and Majestic has borrowed "light" for truth, the Qur'an and proof in several places of the revelation.

* Benefits:
- The blast of the Trumpet (nafkhat al-ṣūr):
al-Ṣūr is the horn, a great realm known only to Allah the Mighty and Majestic; in it are the abodes of the souls of creation. The verse indicates that the blasts number two: the first for swooning (ṣaʿq), that is (death), and the second for resurrection, that is, rising from the graves. But the majority of scholars hold that the blasts are three, the third being the blast of terror (nafkhat al-fazaʿ), which precedes the blast of swooning, by the evidence of His saying, the Exalted: «وَيَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ فَفَزِعَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ».
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Between the two blasts there are forty." They said: "Forty days?" He said: "I refuse (to say)." They said: "Forty months?" He said: "I refuse." They said: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse." Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic sends down water from the sky, and they sprout as vegetables sprout. There is nothing of the human being that does not decay, except one bone, which is (ʿajb al-dhanab, the tailbone), and from it creation will be reassembled on the Day of Resurrection.
And ʿajb al-dhanab is:
a bone like a mustard seed at the end of the coccyx. The scholars hold that between the two blasts there are forty years, and Allah knows best. After the bodies of the servants have sprouted, the final blast is blown in the Trumpet, and the souls fly out from the Trumpet to the bodies, with no soul missing its owner, and they rise alive for the reckoning. That is the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: «وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ», that is, the soul returned to the body, and Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:71-71.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (إلى جهنّم) attached to (سيق). (زمرا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative. (حتّى) a particle of commencement (ibtidāʾ). (لهم) attached to (قال). (الهمزة) for rebuking interrogation. (منكم) attached to an adjective of رسل. (عليكم) attached to (يتلون). (لقاء) second direct object, accusative. (هذا) demonstrative, adjective of (يوم), in the position of the genitive. (بلى) a particle of response affirming a negated question. (الواو) for resumption. (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative. (على الكافرين) attached to (حقّت).
Clause: «سيق الذين ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause وفّيت كلّ نفس «[Note: in the preceding verse (70); it is also permissible that it be cut off as resumptive in the first place.]».
And the clause: «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «جاءوها..» in the position of the genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «فتحت أبوابها ... » has no grammatical position; apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «قال لهم خزنتها ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause فتحت أبوابها.
And the clause: «ألم يأتكم رسل....» in the position of the accusative; the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «يتلون ... » in the position of the accusative; ḥāl from رسل «[Note: or a second adjective of رسل, in the position of the nominative.]».
And the clause: «ينذرونكم ... » in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلون.
And the clause: «قالوا....» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī). The quoted speech is omitted, i.e. "Yes, the messengers came to us."
And the clause: «حقّت كلمة العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Morphology:
(زمرا): plural of زمرة, a collective noun (ism jamʿ) derived from al-zamr, which is sound (ṣawt); its wazn is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn, and the wazn of زمر is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa.
(خزنتها): plural of خازن, active participle from the triliteral خزن; its wazn is فاعل, and the wazn of خزنة is فعلة with three fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(خالدين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the agent of ادخلوا. (فيها) attached to خالدين. (الفاء) resumptive; the specified subject of praise/blame (makhṣūṣ) of بئس is omitted, its implied form being "هي", that is, جهنّم.
Clause: «قيل ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «ادخلوا ... » in the position of the nominative; deputy agent «[Note: because in origin it is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).]».
And the clause: «بئس مثوى ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

safi-cedvel:73-73.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (إلى الجنّة) attached to (سيق). (الواو) conjunction, or circumstantial, or redundant (zāʾida). (لهم) attached to (قال). (سلام) mubtadaʾ, nominative «[Note: the indefinite here indicates praise.]». (عليكم) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ سلام. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition. (خالدين) ḥāl, accusative, from the agent of ادخلوها.
Clause: «سيق الذين ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive «[Note: or conjoined to the clause: سيق الذين.. in verse (71) of this sūra.]».
And the clause: «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «جاءوها..» in the position of the genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «فتحت ... » in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause جاءوها «[Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl with "qad" implied, if the apodosis is taken to be "they came to it, and it had been opened", that is, it is qualified by the ḥāl, which is sound; and it is permissible that it be the apodosis of the condition, with the wāw redundant, which is the opinion of the Kufans.]», the apodosis of the condition being omitted, its implied form being "they were reassured" or "they were happy" ...
And the clause: «قال لهم خزنتها ... » in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause جاءوها.
And the clause: «سلام عليكم ... » in the position of the accusative; maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «طبتم..» has no grammatical position; a resumption within the scope of the speech.
And the clause: «ادخلوها ... » in the position of the jussive; apodosis of an implied condition, that is, "if you enter it, then enter it..".

safi-cedvel:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (لله) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الحمد. (الذي) relative noun in the position of the genitive; adjective of the Name of Majesty (Allah). (من الجنّة) attached to (نتبوّأ). (حيث) adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, attached to (نتبوّأ). (فنعم أجر العاملين) like فبئس مثوى المتكبّرين «[Note: in verse (72) of this sūra]»; and the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is الجنّة.
Clause: «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so they entered it and said ..."
And the clause: «الحمد لله ... » in the position of the accusative; maqūl al-qawl.
And the clause: «صدقنا ... » has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «أورثنا ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «نتبّوأ ... » in the position of the accusative; ḥāl from the first-person pronoun in (أورثنا).
And the clause: «نشاء ... » in the position of the genitive; muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «نعم أجر ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Benefits:
- حيث:
The tribe of Ṭayyiʾ says (حوث). It is indeclinable on ḍamma, though some of the Arabs decline it. And the reading of the one who read (من حيث لا يشعرون). It is by agreement an adverb of place; al-Akhfash said: it may also occur for time. Most often it is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial, or in the genitive after مِن; it may also be put in the genitive by other than that, as in the saying of Zuhayr:
فشد ولم يفزع بيوتا كثيرة ... لدى حيث ألقت رحلها أمّ قشعم
(So he charged, and did not terrify many tents, near where Umm Qashʿam laid down her baggage.)
The point of citation: حيث came in the position of the genitive by annexation after لدى, and the pronoun in the verb شد refers to Ḥuṣayn ibn Ḍamḍam, one of the two instigators of the war of Dāḥis and al-Ghabrāʾ; and Umm Qashʿam is:
death.
Sometimes حيث occurs as a direct object, among which is His saying, the Exalted, in the verse we are dealing with: «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَنا وَعْدَهُ وَأَوْرَثَنَا الْأَرْضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ حَيْثُ نَشاءُ فَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعامِلِينَ», and among which is His saying, the Exalted: «اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ حَيْثُ يَجْعَلُ رِسالَتَهُ», since the meaning is that He, the Exalted, knows the very place deserving of the placing of the message in it, not something in the place; its governing verb is an omitted يعلم indicated by أعلم, not أعلم itself, because the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) does not govern a direct object.
حيث must be annexed to a clause, nominal or verbal, its annexation to a verbal one being more frequent; hence the accusative is preferred in such as (جلست حيث زيدا أراه). When the neutralising ما is attached to it, it takes on the sense of the condition and jazms two verbs, as in the poet's saying:
حيثما تستقم يقدر لك الله ... نجاحا في غابر الأزمان
(Wherever you go straight, Allah will decree success for you in times to come.)
This verse is evidence of its occurring for time.

safi-cedvel:75-75.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (من حول) attached to حافّين. (بحمد) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يسبّحون. (بينهم) adverbial accusative attached to (قضي). (بالحقّ) deputy agent. (لله) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الحمد. (ربّ) adjective of the Name of Majesty (Allah), genitive.
Clause: «ترى ... » has no grammatical position; resumptive.
And the clause: «يسبّحون..» in the position of the accusative; ḥāl from the pronoun in حافّين.
And the clause: «قضي ... بالحقّ» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ترى «[Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl with "qad" implied.]».
And the clause: «قيل ... » has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause ترى.
And the clause: «الحمد لله ... » in the position of the nominative; deputy agent «[Note: because in origin it is the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).]».

* Morphology:
(حافّين): plural of حافّ, active participle from (حفّ) بالشيء, "he surrounded it"; its wazn is فاعل, its ʿayn and lām being one letter ... It was said that (حافّين) has no singular, because surrounding a thing occurs only from a group; this saying is rejected by the reality of things.
(حول): a noun indicating an adverb of place; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn ...

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial; (الفاء) a conjunction; (من) a relative noun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "like him who is safe from it"; (بوجهه) attached to (يتّقي); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يتّقي); (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl; (للظالمين) attached to (قيل); (ما) a relative in the position of accusative, direct object, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of what you were" [Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being a direct object with an omitted muḍāf..], and the returning pronoun is omitted.
Clause: «من يتّقي ... كمن أمن» has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "Are all people equal? Then he who guards...".
And the clause: «يتّقي ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «قيل» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl, with an implied (قد) [Note: or it is conjoined to the clause (يتّقي) and so has no position, i.e. "it will be said to the wrongdoers"; the past form indicates certainty and occurrence.].
And the clause: «ذوقوا ... » is in the position of nominative, deputy agent [Note: because it is originally the content of the saying.].
And the clause: «كنتم تكسبون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «تكسبون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كنتم).

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (kināya): in the words of the Exalted «أَفَمَنْ يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ».
Guarding oneself with the face is a metonymy for the absence of anything to guard oneself with, for guarding oneself with the face has no sense, since one cannot guard with it and it does not escape being scratched. What one guards with are the two hands, and they are shackled to his neck. It is also said: it is an analogical figurative expression (majāz tamthīlī), because the one thrown into the Fire did not intend to guard with his face, but he found nothing to guard with other than his face, and had he found it he would have done so; so when he met it with his face, his state was the state of one guarding with his face, and this was expressed as guarding, by way of analogical figuration.

safi-cedvel:25-26.t:
* I'rab:
(من قبلهم) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of the relative; (الفاء) a conjunction in both places; (حيث) a noun indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive by the preposition, attached to (أتاهم); (لا) negative.
Clause: «كذّب الذين ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «أتاهم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «لا يشعرون» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
(26) (في الحياة) attached to (أذاقهم) [Note: or to an omitted element, a ḥāl from the object.]; (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of commencement, for emphasis; (لو) a conditional particle that does not govern the jussive.
And the clause: «أذاقهم الله ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (أتاهم العذاب).
And the clause: «عذاب الآخرة أكبر» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «كانوا يعلمون ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: it may be a ḥāl from the object pronoun in (أذاقهم) ...], and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "they would not have denied their messengers in this world".
And the clause: «يعلمون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).

safi-cedvel:27-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of confirmation; (للناس) attached to (ضربنا); (في هذا) attached to (ضربنا); (القرآن) badal from (ذا), or ʿaṭf bayān to it, genitive; (من كلّ) attached to (ضربنا)..
Clause: «ضربنا ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the implied oath, and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «لعلّهم يتذكّرون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption, or a clause of justification.
And the clause: «يتذكّرون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (لعلّهم).
(28) (قرآنا) an accusative ḥāl, preparatory (muwaṭṭiʾa), or emphatic of the word (القرآن) [Note: what justified a rigid noun serving as ḥāl is that it is qualified; so it is preparatory to the ḥāl which, in meaning, is (عربيّا); and it may be a direct object of the operator (يتذكّرون).]; (غير) a second adjective of (قرآنا), accusative.. or a ḥāl.
And the clause: «لعلّهم يتّقون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption, or a justification for making the Qur'an Arabic.
And the clause: «يتّقون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (لعل).

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in the words of the Exalted «عِوَجٍ».
The word crookedness (ʿiwaj) is specific to abstract meanings, not to concrete things. It is also said that what is meant by crookedness is doubt and confusion.
He recited:
وقد أتاك يقين غير ذي عوج ... من الإله وقول غير مكذوب
(Certainty free of crookedness has come to you from the Deity, and a word that is not falsified.)
So (العوج) is an explicit metaphor.
2- Reversed simile (tashbīh maqlūb): in the words of the Exalted «أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ كَالْمُفْسِدِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الْمُتَّقِينَ كَالْفُجَّارِ».
The original form of the speech is: "Shall We make the corrupters like the reformers, and the immoral like the God-fearing?", but it was reversed, for emphasis and to go along with the disbelievers' assumption that they are higher in rank than the believing God-fearing in the Hereafter, just as they are in this world, because the norm is that the lower is likened to the higher.

* Benefits:
- The divisions of the ḥāl:
It is divided according to several considerations:
1- The first: its division according to whether its meaning is transient or inseparable, into two kinds: transient (muntaqila), which is the most common, and inseparable (mulāzima), and this is obligatory in three cases:
The first of them: the rigid noun not interpreted as a derived one, such as (هذا مالك ذهبا) ("this is your property, as gold") and (هذه جبّتك خزّا) ("this is your cloak, as silk"), in contrast to a case such as (بعته يدا بيد) ("I sold it hand to hand"), meaning "with mutual handing over", which is a transient attribute. It is not interpreted in the first because it is used in its original sense, unlike in the second. Many imagine that a rigid ḥāl can only be one interpreted as a derived word, but that is not so.
The second: the emphatic, such as (وَلَّى مُدْبِراً) and your saying (هو الحق صادقا) ("it is the truth, truthfully"), because truthfulness is among the necessary concomitants and attributes of truth.
The third: that whose operator indicates the renewal of its owner, such as (خُلِقَ الْإِنْسانُ ضَعِيفاً) and their saying (خلق الله الزرافة يديها أطول من رجليها) ("Allah created the giraffe with its forelegs longer than its hind legs").
2- The second: its division according to whether it is intended for itself or as a preparation, into two kinds: intended (maqṣūda), which is the most common, and preparatory (muwaṭṭiʾa), which is the rigid one that is qualified, such as (فَتَمَثَّلَ لَها بَشَراً سَوِيًّا).
He mentioned (بشرا) only as a preparation for mentioning (سويا), and you say: (جاءني زيد رجلا محسنا) ("Zayd came to me as a benevolent man"). Likewise the words of the Exalted in the verse before us (قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا): (قرآنا) is a ḥāl from the word (القرآن) in the preceding verse and is a preparatory ḥāl, so (قرآنا) is mentioned as a preparation for mentioning (عربيا). We saw in this example how the ḥāl in meaning is the adjective that came after the preparatory ḥāl, for the word (عربيا) is the ḥāl in meaning, not in i'rab.
3- The third: its division according to time into three: concurrent (muqārina), which is the most common, as in the words of the Exalted «وَهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً»; anticipated (muqaddara), as in the words of the Exalted «فَادْخُلُوها خالِدِينَ» and «لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرامَ إِنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُؤُسَكُمْ», i.e. that being anticipated in the future; and recounted (maḥkiyya), which is the past, such as (جاء زيد أمس راكبا) ("Zayd came yesterday riding").
4- The fourth: its division according to clarification and emphasis into two kinds: clarifying (mubayyina), which is the most common and is also called founding (muʾassisa), and emphatic (muʾakkida), which is that whose meaning is understood without it, and it is of three kinds:
a- emphatic of its operator, as in the words of the Exalted «وَلَّى مُدْبِراً»; b- emphatic of the content of the sentence: such as (زيد أبوك عطوفا) ("Zayd is your father, compassionately"); c- and emphatic of its owner, such as: «جاء القوم طرّا» ("the people came, all together") and the words of the Exalted: «لَآمَنَ مَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً».

safi-cedvel:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(رجلا) badal from (مثلا), accusative; (فيه) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (شركاء); (لرجل) attached to (سلم); (هل) an interrogative particle; (مثلا) tamyīz, accusative; (لله) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الحمد); (بل) for transitional rejection (iḍrāb intiqālī); (لا) negative..
Clause: «ضرب الله ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يستويان ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «الحمد لله ... » has no grammatical position, a parenthetical clause of praise.
And the clause: «أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «لا يعلمون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).

* Morphology:
(متشاكسون): plural of (متشاكس), an active participle from the quinquiliteral verb (تشاكس), on the pattern متفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(سلما): the maṣdar of the triliteral (سلم له) in the pattern of فرح, used as an attribute by way of exaggeration, or with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing wholeness" (ذا سلم).

* Rhetoric:
The art of the proverb (mathal): in the words of the Exalted «ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكاءُ مُتَشاكِسُونَ».
In the verse is the art of the proverb sent forth (irsāl al-mathal). He likened the state of one who worships various gods to a slave owned jointly by partners among whom a fierce dispute has arisen and open quarrelling, each pulling him his way, while he stands bewildered, not knowing to which of them to turn, to which to submit, or which of them is more deserving of his obedience; and the state of one who worships one God, who is wholly devoted to His service, answers all His needs, and listens attentively to everything He assigns to him and asks of him.

safi-cedvel:30-31.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (تختصمون), and likewise the accusative adverb (عند)..
Clause: «إنّك ميّت ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «إنّهم ميّتون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «إنّكم ... تختصمون» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «إنّهم ميّتون».
And the clause: «تختصمون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (إنّكم).

* Benefits:
Retribution on the Day of Resurrection:
This verse shows that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection will exact retribution from the wrongdoer for the wronged, and from the falsifier for the one in the right, as
Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: when «ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ» was revealed, al-Zubayr said:
"O Messenger of Allah, will the quarrel be held against us after what happened between us in the world?" He said: "Yes." He said:
"Then the matter is truly severe." Related by al-Tirmidhī
who said: a good and sound ḥadīth. Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "We lived a period of time thinking that this verse was revealed about us and the People of the two Books. We said: how shall we quarrel when our religion is one and our book is one? until I saw some of us striking one another's faces with the sword, and I knew that it was revealed about us."
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do you know who is the bankrupt?" They said: "The bankrupt among us is the one who has no dirham and no goods." He said:
"The bankrupt of my community is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and zakāt, and comes having insulted this one, slandered that one, consumed the property of another, shed the blood of another, and struck another. So this one is given from his good deeds, and that one from his good deeds. If his good deeds run out before he has settled what he owes, some of their sins are taken and cast upon him, and then he is cast into the Fire." Related by Muslim.
Part Twenty-Four
The remainder of Sūrat al-Zumar
from verse 32 to verse 75; Sūrat Ghāfir, its verses 85; Sūrat Fuṣṣilat from verse 1 to verse 42

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (أظلم); (ممّن) attached to (أظلم); (على الله) attached to (كذب); (الواو) a conjunction; (بالصّدق) attached to (كذّب); (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of accusative, attached to (كذّب); (الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation; (في جهنّم) attached to an omitted element, the predicate of (ليس); (مثوى) the postponed noun of (ليس), nominative; (للكافرين) attached to (مثوى).
Clause: «من أظلم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «كذب ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «كذّب ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
And the clause: «جاءه ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ليس في جهنّم مثوى ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:33-35.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (بالصدق) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (جاء) [Note: or attached to (جاء), being an adjective of an omitted described noun, i.e. "he came with truthful speech".]; (به) attached to (صدّق); (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); (المتّقون) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
Clause: «الذي جاء ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «جاء بالصدق ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
And the clause: «صدّق به ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (جاء) ...
And the clause: «أولئك.. المتّقون..» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذي).. [Note: it is possible that the clause (هم المتقون), consisting of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك)..
And it is possible that the clause (أولئك.. المتقون) is a ḥāl from the agent of (جاء), and the clause (لهم ما يشاءون) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذي).] (34) (لهم) attached to an omitted element, a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (ما); (عند) an accusative adverb attached to a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun or from the agent of (يشاءون).. and the reference in (ذلك) is to what they desire..
And the clause: «لهم ما يشاءون ... » is in the position of nominative, a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك) ...
And the clause: «يشاءون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «ذلك جزاء ... » has no grammatical position, a clause of justification.
(35) (اللام) the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba); (يكفّر) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām; (عنهم) attached to (يكفّر); (الذي) a relative, muḍāf ilayhi in the position of genitive; (الواو) a conjunction; (يجزيهم) accusative, conjoined to (يكفّر); (أجرهم) second direct object, accusative; (بأحسن) attached to (يجزيهم); and the returning pronoun of (الذي) is omitted, i.e. "which they did" (يعملونه).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يكفّر ... ) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He made that easy for them" [Note: or attached to (المحسنين), as if it were said: "those who did good so as to have expiation".].
And the clause: «يكفّر الله ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause: «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the first relative (الذي).
And the clause: «يجزيهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «يكفّر الله ...».
And the clause: «كانوا يعملون..» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (الذي).
And the clause: «يعملون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).

* Morphology:
(أسوأ): a comparative noun from the triliteral (ساء), and the weak letter returned to its origin; its pattern is أفعل.

safi-cedvel:36-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation; (كاف) genitive in form, accusative in position, the predicate of (ليس), the genitive marker being the implied kasra on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); (عبده) direct object of the active participle (كاف); (الواو) resumptive in the first two places and conjunctive in the third; (بالذين) attached to (يخوّفونك); (من دونه) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of the relative; (من) a conditional noun governing the jussive, in the position of accusative, a fronted direct object; (يضلل) given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (ما) negative, inoperative [Note: or operating as (ليس), the preposition and its genitive noun being the predicate of (ما) and (هاد) nominative in position, the postponed noun of (ما).]; (له) attached to a fronted predicate; (هاد) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ, the genitive marker being like that of (كاف).
Clause: «أليس الله بكاف..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يخوّفونك..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يضلل الله ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «ما له من هاد..» is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the (فاء).
(37) (من يهد ... من مضل) like «من يضلل.. من هاد»; (أليس الله بعزيز) like «أليس الله بكاف»; (ذي) an adjective of (عزيز), genitive in form, the genitive marker being the yāʾ.
And the clause: «من يهد الله ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «يضلل الله».
And the clause: «ما له من مضلّ....» is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the (فاء).
And the clause: «أليس الله بعزيز..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(كاف): an active participle from the triliteral (كفى), on the pattern فاع, with a weakening by deletion to suit the tanwīn, so it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).

safi-cedvel:38-38.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) preparatory to the oath; (سألتهم) a past verb, indeclinable, in the position of jussive, the protasis; (من) an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ [Note: or it is a relative noun in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "about who created...."]; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يقولنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative for being free of governing particles, the nominative marker being the presence of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of similar letters, and the omitted (الواو), dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the agent, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (الله) the Majestic Name, mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, i.e. "their Creator"; (الهمزة) interrogative; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition, and (أرأيتم) means "inform me"; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative, first direct object; (من دون) attached to a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun, i.e. "that you invoke"; (أراد) like (سألت), and the (النون) in it is the protective nūn; (بضرّ) attached to (أرادني); (هل) an interrogative particle; (أو) a conjunction; (برحمة) attached to the second (أرادني); (حسبي) a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الله); (عليه) attached to (يتوكّل)..
Clause: «إن سألتهم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «من خلق ... » is in the position of accusative, direct object of the verb of asking, which is suspended by the interrogative, with the preposition implied.
And the clause: «خلق ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
And the clause: «يقولنّ..» has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
And the clause: «لله (خالقهنّ) ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «قل....» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «رأيتم..» is in the position of jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "If Allah wills harm or benefit for me, then tell me whether they would ward off my harm or withhold my benefit" [Note: or it has no position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition: "if there were another god besides Him, tell me whether he would ward off harm that Allah willed or withhold benefit that Allah decreed ..."], and the condition clause, its verb and its apodosis are the content of the saying.
And the clause: «تدعون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «أرادني ... » has no grammatical position, parenthetical.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes.
And the clause: «هل هنّ كاشفات ... » is in the position of accusative, second direct object, the operator being (أرأيتم).
And the clause: «أرادني (الثانية) » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (أرادني) (the first).
And the clause: «هل هنّ ممسكات ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause «هل هن كاشفات».
And the clause: «قل....» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «حسبي الله ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «يتوكّل المتوكّلون» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(ممسكات): plural of (ممسكة), feminine of (ممسك), an active participle from the quadriliteral (أمسك).. see verse (2) of Sūrat Fāṭir.

safi-cedvel:39-40.t:
* I'rab:
(قوم) the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative, the accusative marker being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the speaker's yāʾ, which was omitted for lightness....
and the omitted (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (على مكانتكم) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (اعملوا); (الفاء) causal ...
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يا قوم ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «اعملوا ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «إنّي عامل ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «سوف تعلمون ... » has no grammatical position, a justification for the command to act.
(40) (من) a relative noun in the position of accusative, direct object, whose operator is (تعلمون); (عليه) attached to (يحلّ) ...
And the clause: «يأتيه عذاب ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «يخزيه ... » is in the position of nominative, an adjective of (عذاب).
And the clause: «يحلّ.. عذاب» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (يخزيه).

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor: in the words of the Exalted «قُلْ يا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ».
For (المكانة) was transferred from the perceptible place to the condition a person is in, and borrowed for it as a borrowing of the perceptible for the intelligible, just as (حيث) and (هنا) are borrowed for time on the basis of the shared sense of inclusion and encompassing. The point of likeness is their firmness in that state, like the firmness of one established in his place.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّا) a particle resembling the verb, and its noun; (عليك) attached to (أنزلنا); (للناس) attached to (أنزلنا), and the (اللام) is causal, i.e. "for the sake of the people"; (بالحقّ) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (أنزلنا) or from its object; (الفاء) a conjunction; (من) a conditional noun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis in both places; (لنفسه) attached to the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "his guidance"; (من ضلّ) like (من اهتدى), each of them in the position of jussive, the protasis; (إنّما) a restricting particle and what it restricts; (عليها) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (يضلّ); (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative, operating as (ليس); (عليهم) attached to (وكيل); (وكيل) genitive in form, accusative in position, the predicate of (ما).
Clause: «إنّا أنزلنا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «أنزلنا ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «من اهتدى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «اهتدى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses, the protasis and the apodosis, together.].
And the clause: « (اهتداؤه) لنفسه.. is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the (فاء).
And the clause: «من ضلّ ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «من اهتدى ...».
And the clause: «ضلّ ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: the khabar may be the two clauses, the protasis and the apodosis, together.].
And the clause: «إنّما يضلّ عليها» is in the position of jussive, the apodosis, joined with the (فاء).
And the clause: «ما أنت عليهم بوكيل» has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or conjoined by the wāw to the clause «إنّما يضلّ عليها», in the position of jussive.].

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(حين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يتوفّى); (الواو) a conjunction; (التي) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined to (الأنفس); (في منامها) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (تمت) [Note: or attached to (يتوفّى).]; (الفاء) a conjunction; (عليها) attached to (قضى); (إلى أجل) attached to (يرسل); (في ذلك) attached to an omitted element, the predicate of inna; (اللام) the lām of commencement, for emphasis; (آيات) the noun of inna, accusative; (لقوم) attached to an adjective of (آيات).
Clause: «الله يتوفّى....» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يتوفّى ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
And the clause: «لم تمت ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (التي).
And the clause: «يمسك ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (يتوفّى).
And the clause: «قضى ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second relative (التي).
And the clause: «يرسل ... » is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause (يمسك).
And the clause: «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ... » has no grammatical position, a clause of justification.
And the clause: «يتفكّرون» is in the position of genitive, an adjective of (قوم).

* Benefits:
The spirit and the body:
This verse made clear that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the One who takes the spirits of servants at death, while the soul that has not died He takes in its sleep. The soul He takes at sleep is the one through which there is intellect and discernment, since every human being has two souls: a soul through which there is life, which leaves him at death, and the other soul through which there is discernment, which leaves him at sleep, and breathing does not cease with its departure. As for the first soul, it is the one Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, withholds, and as for the second, it is the one He sends back on waking. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib said: the spirit goes out at sleep and its ray remains in the body, and by that he sees the dream; so when he wakes from sleep the spirit returns to the body in less than a moment. It is also said: the spirits of the living and the dead meet in sleep and become acquainted as much as Allah the Exalted wills; then when they want to return to their bodies, Allah the Exalted withholds the spirits of the dead and sends back the spirits of the living.
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you retires to his bed, let him dust off his bed with the inner part of his lower garment, for he does not know what has come to be on it after him; then let him say:
In Your name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and by You I raise it; if You withhold my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, protect it with that with which You protect Your righteous servants."
If you ask: how are the words of the Exalted «اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِها» reconciled with His words «قُلْ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ مَلَكُ الْمَوْتِ الَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ»? The answer: the One who truly takes is Allah the Exalted, and the angel of death is the one who seizes the spirit by the permission of Allah the Exalted; the angel of death has helpers who assist him in carrying out the task. It is also said: the earth is folded for him until it becomes like a bowl before him, to ease the performance of the task. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(تنزيل) is a mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and (من الله) is attached to the maṣdar تنزيل.]; (من الله) is attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ تنزيل.
Clause: «تنزيل الكتاب من الله ...» has no grammatical position; it is an inceptive clause.

safi-cedvel:2-2.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّا) is a particle resembling the verb, and its ism; (إليك) is attached to (أنزلنا); (بالحقّ) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of أنزلنا [Note: or to a ḥāl from الكتاب.. It is also permissible to attach it to the verb أنزلنا, with the bāʾ of causation.]; (الفاء) is a conjunction connecting the effect with the cause; (مخلصا) is a ḥāl from the agent of اعبد; (له) is attached to (مخلصا); (الدين) is a direct object of the active participle.
Clause: «إنّا أنزلنا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أنزلنا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «اعبد ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e. "Take heed, and worship".

safi-cedvel:3-3.t:
* I'rab:
(ألا) is for alerting; (لله) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ الدين; (الواو) (الواو) is resumptive; (من دونه) is attached to an omitted second direct object; (ما) is negative; (إلّا) is for restriction; (اللام) is for giving a reason; (يقرّبوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (إلى الله) is attached to (يقرّبونا); (زلفى) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar because it is its synonym [Note: Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed it to be an emphatic ḥāl.].
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يقرّبونا ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (نعبدهم).
(بينهم) is an accusative adverb attached to (يحكم); (في ما) is attached to (يحكم); (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون); (لا) is negative.
Clause: «لله الدين ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «الذين اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «ما نعبدهم ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying of an implied saying, i.e.: "they say: we do not worship them ...."
And the implied saying clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
And the clause «يقرّبونا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied literal particle (أن).
And the clause «إنّ الله يحكم ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «يحكم ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «هم فيه يختلفون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «يختلفون ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.
And the clause «إنّ الله لا يهدي من ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يهدي من ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «هو كاذب ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).

safi-cedvel:4-6.t:
* I'rab:
(لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle; (اللام) occurs in the apodosis of لو; (ممّا) is attached to (اصطفى), and the returning pronoun is omitted [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the second relative noun (ما).]; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object, and the returning pronoun is omitted.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يتّخذ ...) is in the position of accusative as a direct object.
(سبحانه) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; (الواحد، القهّار) are two adjectives of the Name of Majesty, nominative.
Clause: «أراد الله ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يتّخذ ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the literal particle (أن).
And the clause «اصطفى ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «يخلق ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (ما).
And the clause «يشاء ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
And the clause «(نسبّح) سبحان ...» has no grammatical position; it is a parenthetical clause of supplication - or an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «هو الله ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
(5) (بالحقّ) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent - or from the object - [Note: and the bāʾ is for accompaniment, or it is attached to (خلق) and the bāʾ is causal.]; (على النهار) is attached to (يكوّر), meaning "makes enter", and likewise (على الليل); (كلّ) is a mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: indicating generality, and the tanwīn is a substitute for something omitted, i.e. "each one of them".]; (لأجل) is attached to (يجري); (ألا) is for alerting.
And the clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumptive [Note: or it is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ الله.].
And the clause «يكوّر ...» has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumptive [Note: or another khabar of the Name of Majesty ... or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of خلق.].
And the clause «يكوّر (the second)» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يكوّر (the first).
And the clause «سخّر ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خلق.
And the clause «كلّ يجري ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the sun and the moon.].
And the clause «هو العزيز ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(6) (من نفس) is attached to (خلقكم); (منها) is attached to (جعل) [Note: by implying in it the meaning of "created" ... or attached to an omitted second direct object if it is among the verbs of transformation.]; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكم) is attached to (أنزل); (من الأنعام) is attached to a ḥāl from ثمانية أزواج; (في بطون) is attached to (يخلقكم); (خلقا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative; (من بعد) is attached to an adjective of (خلقا) [Note: or attached to (يخلقكم)]; (في ظلمات) is a badal from (في بطون) with repetition of the preposition, so it is attached to (يخلقكم) [Note: or attached to (خلق), which is mentioned before it.]; (الله), the Name of Majesty, is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلكم; (ربّكم) is a second khabar, nominative; (له) is attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الملك); (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (إلّا) is for exception; (هو) is a detached pronoun, a badal from the pronoun in the omitted khabar, in the position of nominative; (الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis; (أنّى) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to a ḥāl from the nāʾib fāʿil in (تصرفون) [Note: أنّى comes with the meaning of كيف.. so on this view it is originally a ḥāl.].
And the clause «خلقكم من نفس ...» has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خلقكم.
And the clause «أنزل لكم ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause خلقكم.
And the clause «يخلقكم ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «ذلكم الله ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «له الملك ...» is in the position of nominative as a third khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلكم.
And the clause «لا إله إلّا هو» is in the position of nominative as a fourth khabar - or resumptive.
And the clause «تصرفون ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if this is the way of Allah, then how are you turned away?"

* Rhetoric:
1- Conjunction with «thumma»: in His saying, the Exalted: «ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْها زَوْجَها».
He conjoined it with thumma to the first sign, to indicate its distinctness from it in excellence and merit, and its remoteness from it in what relates to its being yet more of a sign; so it is a remoteness in state and rank, not a remoteness in existence.
2- Al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya (derivative metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: «وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَنْعامِ ثَمانِيَةَ أَزْواجٍ». The "sending down" is a majāz for decree and apportionment: for when He, the Exalted, decrees and apportions, He records that in the Preserved Tablet, and the angels charged with bringing it to light come down with it. He described it with descent although it is a common, familiar meaning, like a literal one. The relation between sending down and decree is emergence after concealment; so in the speech there is a derivative metaphor, and it is possible that it is a majāz mursal.

* Benefits:
1- Artistic depiction in the Noble Qur'an:
The divine statement, in this verse, has made of the image of the succession of night and day a vivid, embodied picture, a picture in which life and movement flow, and lines and colours pulse. So He, the Exalted, said: «يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ». The meaning of takwīr is winding; it is said: "he wound (kāra) the turban on his head and coiled it (kawwarahā)." Al-Zamakhsharī says that night and day succeed one another: this one goes away and that one covers its place. From here we grasp the extent of the depiction and movement in the image of night and day and their succession with the days, and we grasp the meaning of takwīr, which produces in the mind and imagination that ceaseless movement, and the winding and revolving which appears to the imagination in the alternation of night and day. So the image is present and the movement constant forever without end, and night and day follow each other in succession without stopping or delay.
2- The three darknesses:
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The three darknesses are: the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta (which is the membrane of the human child). When a person stands contemplating and reflecting on his growth in the womb and his stages in these three darknesses, and how the care of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, surrounds him so that he is completed in his mother's belly for nine months, and then comes as a newborn into this existence, he can do nothing but fall down prostrate before the greatness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His mighty power which watched over him and brought him forth as a well-formed creature in three darknesses.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis; (عنكم) is attached to غنيّ; (الواو) is a conjunction; (لعباده) is attached to (يرضى); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لكم) is attached to (يرضه); (الواو) is resumptive; (لا) is negative; (وزارة) is an adjective standing in for the described noun, i.e. "a soul that bears"; and likewise (أخرى); (إلى ربّكم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ مرجعكم; (الفاء); (ما) is a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of genitive, and the returning pronoun is omitted.]; (بذات) is attached to عليم.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم ...) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (ينبّئكم).
Clause: «تكفروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

And the clause «لا يرضى ...» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar غنيّ.
And the clause «تشكروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تكفروا.
And the clause «يرضه ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of the condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause «لا تزر وازرة ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the resumptive clause.].
And the clause «إلى ربّكم مرجعكم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
And the clause «ينبّئكم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the last nominal clause.
And the clause «كنتم تعملون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the literal - or the relative - noun.
And the clause «تعملون ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم.
And the clause «إنّه عليم» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), meaning (بل); (من دون) attached to an omitted element, second direct object, whose operator is (اتّخذوا); (الهمزة) interrogative; (الواو) of ḥāl; (لو) a conditional particle that does not govern the jussive; (لا) negative; (شيئا) direct object, accusative, i.e. anything of intercession or otherwise; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) negative.
Clause: «اتّخذوا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive, and the content of the saying is omitted, its implied form being "Would they intercede...".
And the clause: «لو كانوا ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the agent of the implied verb, and the apodosis is omitted, explained by what precedes.

And the clause: «لا يعقلون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause (لا يملكون).

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(لله) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (الشفاعة); (جميعا) a ḥāl from (الشفاعة) [Note: as if intercession were of various kinds, or because it issues from various intercessors], and the operator in it is the sense of being established; (له) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (ملك); (إليه) attached to (ترجعون), and the (الواو) in the verb is the deputy agent.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «لله الشفاعة....» is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «له ملك السموات ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «إليه ترجعون..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (له ملك).

safi-cedvel:45-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (وحده) a ḥāl from the Majestic Name, accusative; (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negative; (بالآخرة) attached to the negated (يؤمنون); (الواو) a conjunction; the second (الذين) is in the position of nominative, deputy agent; (من دونه) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of (الذين); (إذا) a particle of suddenness.
Clause: «ذكر الله ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.

And the clause: «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).

And the clause: «هم يستبشرون» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

safi-cedvel:46-46.t:
* I'rab:
(اللهم) the one addressed, a singular proper noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and the doubled (الميم) is a substitute for the omitted vocative (يا); (فاطر) an adjective of the Majestic Name, accusative because it is a muḍāf [Note: according to Sībawayh it is a second one addressed whose vocative particle was omitted, accusative because it is a muḍāf.]; (عالم) a second adjective, accusative; (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (تحكم); (في ما) attached to (تحكم); (فيه) attached to (يختلفون).
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the vocative clause ... is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «أنت تحكم ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «تحكم ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (أنت).
And the clause: «كانوا فيه يختلفون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «يختلفون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).

safi-cedvel:47-51.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لو) a conditional particle that does not govern the jussive; (للذين) attached to an omitted element, the khabar of anna; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, the noun of anna; (في الأرض) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of (ما); (جميعا) an accusative ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun in the ṣila; (الواو) a conjunction; (مثله) conjoined to the relative (ما), accusative; (معه) an accusative adverb attached to a ḥāl from (مثله)..
