(اللام) occurring in the answer to (لو); (به) attached to (افتدوا); (من سوء) attached to (افتدوا); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (افتدوا); (الواو) a conjunction; (لهم) attached to (بدا); (من الله) attached to (بدا); (ما) a relative in the position of nominative, agent of (بدا).
Clause: « (ثبت) تملّك ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «افتدوا ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «بدا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (افتدوا).
And the clause: «لم يكونوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).
And the clause: «يحتسبون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (يكونوا)..
(48) (الواو) a conjunction; (لهم) attached to the second (بدا); (ما) a relative in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi [Note: or a maṣdar particle, the interpreted maṣdar being muḍāf ilayhi]; (بهم) attached to (حاق); (ما) a relative in the position of nominative, agent of (حاق); (به) attached to (يستهزئون), and the pronoun in (به) refers to the punishment.
And the clause: «بدا لهم سيّئات ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (بدا) (the first).
And the clause: «كسبوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the third relative (ما).
And the clause: «حاق بهم ما ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (بدا) ...
And the clause: «كانوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the fourth relative (ما).
And the clause: «يستهزئون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).
(49) (الفاء) a conjunction; (الإنسان) a fronted direct object; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (منّا) attached to an adjective of (نعمة); (إنّما) a restricting particle and what it restricts; (على علم) attached to a ḥāl from the deputy agent in (أوتيته) [Note: or attached to (أوتيته) if it means: "with knowledge from Allah that I am deserving of it"]; (بل) for transitional rejection; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) negative..
And the clause: «مسّ.. ضرّ» is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «دعانا ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «خوّلناه ... » is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قال ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «أوتيته ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «هي فتنة ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive, or parenthetical. And the clause: «لكنّ أكثرهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «هي فتنة».
And the clause: «لا يعلمون ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of (لكنّ).
(50) (قد) a particle of confirmation; (من قبلهم) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of the relative; (الفاء) a conjunction; (ما) negative; (عنهم) attached to (أغنى); (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of nominative, with the returning pronoun omitted].
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا....) is in the position of nominative, agent of (أغنى)..
And the clause: «قالها الذين....» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «ما أغنى.. ما كانوا....» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (قالها) ...
And the clause: «كانوا....» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the clause: «يكسبون» is in the position of accusative, the khabar of (كانوا).
(51) (الفاء) a conjunction; (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of genitive, with the returning pronoun omitted] in both places; (الواو) a conjunction; (من هؤلاء) attached to a ḥāl from the agent of (ظلموا); (السين) a particle of futurity; (الواو) of ḥāl; (ما) negative, operating as (ليس); (معجزين) genitive in form, accusative in position, the predicate of (ما).
And the clause: «أصابهم سيّئات ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «ما أغنى..».
And the clause: «كسبوا ... (in both places)» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما), first and second.
And the first interpreted maṣdar (ما كسبوا..) is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the second interpreted maṣdar (ما كسبوا ... ) is in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «سيصيبهم سيّئات ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
And the clause: «ما هم بمعجزين» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:52-52.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) interrogative; (الواو) a conjunction; (لمن) attached to (يبسط); (في ذلك) attached to the khabar of inna; (اللام) for emphasis; (لقوم) attached to an adjective of (آيات) ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يبسط..) is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of (يعملوا).
Clause: «يعلموا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.:
"Were they heedless and did not know ..."
And the clause: «يبسط ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of anna.
And the clause: «يشاء ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).
And the clause: «يقدر....» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (يشاء).
And the clause: «إنّ في ذلك لآيات ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «يؤمنون ... » is in the position of genitive, an adjective of (قوم).

safi-cedvel:53-53.t:
* I'rab:
(عبادي) the one addressed, a muḍāf, accusative, the accusative marker being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative, an adjective of (عبادي); (على أنفسهم) attached to (أسرفوا); (لا) prohibitive, governing the jussive; (من رحمة) attached to (تقنطوا); (جميعا) an accusative ḥāl from (الذنوب); (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ [Note: or borrowed for the position of accusative, an emphasis of the attached pronoun, the noun of inna, and the khabar of inna is (الغفور)]; (الغفور) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو)..
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يا عبادي ... » is in the position of accusative, the content of the saying.
And the clause: «أسرفوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «لا تقنطوا ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «إنّ الله يغفر ... » has no grammatical position, a clause of justification.
And the clause: «يغفر ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.
And the clause: «إنّه هو الغفور ... » has no grammatical position, a justification of the preceding justification.
And the clause: «هو الغفور ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.

* Rhetoric:
In the words of the Exalted «قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا.. إلخ», the verse contains many and varied arts of the sciences of badīʿ and bayān:
1- Attributing mercy to the Majestic Name, which comprises all the meanings of the Names, by way of shift of person (iltifāt).
2- Putting the Majestic Name in the place of the pronoun, to signal that forgiveness is among the requirements of His Essence.
3- The shift from first person to third person in the words of the Exalted «من رحمة الله», to specify mercy to the Noble Name.
4- The expression with (الغفور), for it is a form of intensification.
5- Presenting the sentence in the words of the Exalted «إنه هو الغفور الرحيم» as emphasised by inna, by the separating pronoun, and by the two attributes entrusted with intensification.

* Benefits:
- The mercy of Allah is vast:
The exegetes said: this is the most hope-inspiring verse in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to Waḥshī calling him to Islam, and he sent back: "How do you call me to your religion when you claim that whoever kills, associates others with Allah or commits fornication will meet a penalty, and the punishment will be doubled for him, and I have done all of that?" So Allah the Exalted revealed «إِلَّا مَنْ تابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صالِحاً». Waḥshī said: "This is a severe condition; perhaps I will not be able to meet it; is there anything else?"
So Allah the Exalted revealed «إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَغْفِرُ أَنْ يُشْرَكَ بِهِ وَيَغْفِرُ ما دُونَ ذلِكَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ». Waḥshī said: "I still see myself in doubt, for I do not know whether He will forgive me or not." So Allah revealed this verse «قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ». Waḥshī said: "Yes, this is it." So he came and embraced Islam.
And on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: these verses were revealed about ʿAyyāsh ibn Abī Rabīʿa, al-Walīd ibn al-Walīd and a group of Muslims who had embraced Islam, then were persecuted and tortured and apostatised from Islam. We used to say: Allah will not accept repentance from these. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote it with his own hand and sent it to this group, and they all embraced Islam and emigrated. No one should think that the meaning of the verse requires a person to give free rein to himself and run after sins and major offences; that is not the case. What is meant is to draw attention to the vastness of the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to revive hope in the hearts of sinners, to urge repentance, and not to cut the rope of hope in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

safi-cedvel:8-9.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (إليه) is attached to the ḥāl (منيبا); (منه) is attached to an adjective of نعمة; (إليه) is attached to (يدعو); (قبل) is an adverbial noun, indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of genitive, attached to (يدعو); (الواو) is a conjunction; (لله) is attached to an omitted second direct object; (اللام) is for giving a reason; (يضلّ) is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (عن سبيله) is attached to (يضلّ).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يضلّ) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (جعل).
(بكفرك) is attached to (تمتّع); (قليلا) is a mafʿūl fīhi, an adverb of time - standing in for the adverb - [Note: or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective.]; (من أصحاب) is attached to the khabar of (إنّ).
Clause: «مسّ.. ضرّ» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.. and the condition, its verb and its apodosis are resumptive.
And the clause «دعا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «خوّله ...» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.. and the condition, its verb and its apodosis are conjoined to the first condition, its verb and its resumptive apodosis.
And the clause «نسي ...» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «كان يدعو ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «يدعو ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كان.
And the clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause نسي.
And the clause «يضل ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the literal particle (أن).
And the clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «تمتّع ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «إنّك من أصحاب ...» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason.
(9) (أم) is for transitional iḍrāb (turning away), meaning بل, with the hamza of rhetorical-denying interrogation; (من) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "like one who is disobedient"; (ساجدا) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in قانت; (هل) is a particle of denying interrogation; (إنّما) is a restrictor and restricted (kāffa and makfūfa)..
Clause: «من هو قانت (كمن هو عاص)» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive within the scope of the preceding saying.
And the clause «هو قانت ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «يحذر ...» is in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl.
And the clause «يرجو ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يحذر.
And the clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «يستوي ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «لا يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «يتذكّر أولو الألباب» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(عباد) is a vocative muḍāf, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ that is omitted for lightness, following the reading in connected speech, and the (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi; (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as an adjective of عباد; (للذين) is attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ حسنة; (في هذه) is attached to (أحسنوا); (إنّما) is a restrictor and restricted (kāffa and makfūfa); (أجرهم) is a direct object of the passive verb يوفّى; (بغير) is attached to a ḥāl from أجرهم.
Clause: «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the vocative clause and its response ... are in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
And the clause «أحسنوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «للذين أحسنوا ... حسنة» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «أرض الله واسعة ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the explanatory resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the response to the vocative.].
And the clause «إنّما يوفّى الصابرون ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive within the scope of the saying.

safi-cedvel:11-12.t:
* I'rab:
The (تاء) in (أمرت) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (أن) is a maṣdar and accusative-governing particle; (له) is attached to (مخلصا); (الدين) is a direct object of the active participle (مخلصا).
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن أعبد) is in the position of accusative as a direct object whose operator is أمرت.
Clause: «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّي أمرت ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «أمرت ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «أعبد ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the literal particle (أن).
(12) (اللام) is for giving a reason - or has the meaning of the bāʾ, for transitivity; (أن أكون) is like أن أعبد.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أمرت).
And the clause «أمرت (the second)» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أمرت (the first).
And the clause «أكون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the literal particle (أن).

safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(عصيت) is an indeclinable past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis verb (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (عذاب) is a direct object, accusative, whose operator is أخاف.
Clause: «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّي أخاف ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «أخاف ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
And the clause «عصيت ...» has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical ... and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

safi-cedvel:60-61.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (ترى); (على الله) attached to (كذبوا); (الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation; (في جهنّم) attached to an omitted element, the predicate of (ليس); (مثوى) the noun of (ليس), nominative, the nominative marker being the implied ḍamma; (للمتكبّرين) attached to an adjective of (مثوى).
Clause: «ترى ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «كذبوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «وجوههم مسودّة ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the relative.
And the clause: «أليس في جهنّم مثوى ... » has no grammatical position, a clause of justification, or a resumption to affirm the content of what precedes.
(61) (الواو) a conjunction; (بمفازتهم) attached to (ينجّي), and the (ب) is causal; (لا) negative in both places ...
And the clause: «ينجّي الله ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (ترى) ...
And the clause: «اتّقوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «لا يمسهم السوء ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from the relative [Note: or it has no position, an explanatory resumption of what precedes.].
And the clause: «هم يحزنون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause «لا يمسهم السوء».
And the clause: «يحزنون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:62-63.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (على كلّ) attached to (وكيل).
Clause: «الله خالق ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «هو ... وكيل» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(63) (له) attached to a fronted predicate of the mubtadaʾ (مقاليد); (الواو) resumptive, or conjunctive; (بآيات) attached to (كفروا); (هم) a separating pronoun, or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الخاسرون), the clause being the khabar of (أولئك).
And the clause: «له مقاليد ... » has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «الذين كفروا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or conjoined to the clause «ينجي الله..» in verse (61), what lies between them being parenthetical.].
And the clause: «كفروا....» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
And the clause: «أولئك ... الخاسرون» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).

* Morphology:
(مقاليد): plural of (مقلاد), a noun of instrument, on the pattern مفتاح with kasra on the mīm, or plural of (مقليد) on the pattern منديل with kasra on the mīm.. it may be a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its own wording.

safi-cedvel:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (غير) a fronted direct object whose operator is (أعبد), and the doubled (النّون) in (تأمرونّي) is the nominative marker together with the protective nūn; (أيّها) the one addressed, an indefinite noun with specific reference, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative; (الجاهلون) badal from (أيّ), or ʿaṭf bayān to it, or an adjective of it, following it in the nominative in form.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «تأمرونّي ... » is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "If Allah is the Creator of everything, how do you command me to worship other than Allah?"
And the clause: «أعبد ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن) [Note: the original form of the speech is «أتأمرونني أن أعبد غير الله»; when the maṣdar particle was omitted the verb became nominative, and no account is taken of the fronting of the object of the ṣila before it, because the maṣdar particle was omitted; and the interpreted maṣdar (أن أعبد ... ) is in the position of accusative, direct object, whose operator is (تأمرونني).].
And the clause: «أيّها الجاهلون» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Benefits:
- The protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya):
Also called the nūn of support (nūn al-ʿimād). It comes before the speaker's yāʾ when that is attached to one of three:
a- The verb, whether inflected, such as «أكرمني», or rigid, such as «عساني» and (قاموا ما خلاني وما عداني وحاشاني) if you take them as verbs. As for the words of Ruʾba:
عددت قومي كعديد الطيس ... إن ذهبت القوم الكرام ليسي
(I counted my people like the number of the sand-dunes, if the noble people are gone, except me)
that is a poetic necessity. The meaning of (الطيس) is abundant sand. And in a form such as (تأمرونني) both the unmerged and the merged forms are permissible, (تأمرونّي), as well as pronouncing a single nūn. They have been recited in these ways among the Seven. As for the last (i.e. the recitation with a single nūn, تأمروني), it is said: the remaining nūn is the nūn of the nominative, and it is said it is the protective nūn, which is the correct view.
b- The second: the verbal noun (ism fiʿl), such as (داركني وتراكني وعليكني) meaning "overtake me", "leave me" and "stay with me".
c- The third: the particle, such as «إنني», and it may be omitted with inna, anna, lākinna and ka-anna; omission is the rule with (لعلّ), and is rare with «ليت». It is also attached before the yāʾ that is genitive after (من) and (عن), except out of necessity.
And before the yāʾ attached as muḍāf ilayhi to ladun, qad or qaṭ, except in a little of speech.

safi-cedvel:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of confirmation; (إليك) attached to (أوحي), and likewise (إلى الذين), which is conjoined to it; (من قبلك) attached to an omitted element, the ṣila of (الذين); (اللام) preparatory to the oath; (إن) a conditional particle governing the jussive; (أشركت) a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis; (اللام) the lām of the oath; (يحبطنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of nominative, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (الواو) a conjunction; (لتكوننّ) like (ليحبطنّ), its noun being a latent pronoun, its implied form being (أنت); (من الخاسرين) attached to the khabar of (تكونّن).
Clause: «أوحي ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «إن أشركت ... » has no grammatical position, explicative of the implied deputy agent [Note: i.e. "monotheism was revealed to you"].
And the clause: «يحبطنّ عملك ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath.
And the clause: «تكوننّ من الخاسرين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the answer to the oath.
(66) (بل) for transitional rejection; (الله) the Majestic Name, a fronted direct object whose operator is (اعبد); (الفاء) a conjunction [Note: it is redundant according to al-Fārisī because a performative clause precedes it and it separated the verb from the object; Ibn Hishām rejected that in al-Mughnī.]; (من الشاكرين) attached to the khabar of (كن).
And the clause: «اعبد ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.:
"Take heed, then worship Allah."
And the clause: «كن من الشاكرين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (اعبد).

safi-cedvel:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (حقّ) an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar; (الواو) of ḥāl; (جميعا) a ḥāl from (الأرض) considering its plural meaning; (قبضته) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الأرض), nominative; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (قبضة) in the sense of "seized"; (الواو) a conjunction; (بيمينه) attached to (مطويّات); (سبحانه) an absolute object, accusative; (عمّا) attached to (تعالى).
Clause: «ما قدروا....» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «الأرض ... قبضته» is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl.
And the clause: «السموات مطويّات ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.
And the clause: « (نسبّح) سبحانه» has no grammatical position, a parenthetical clause of praise, or resumptive. And the clause: «تعالى ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause «(نسبّح) سبحانه».
And the clause: «يشركون» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(قبضة): a noun for the cupped palm, used here figuratively in the sense of dominion and power and in the sense of "seized", or in the sense of "perishing, non-existent"; its pattern is فعلة, the pattern of the maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar al-marra) of the verb (قبض).
(مطويّات): plural of (مطويّة), feminine of (مطويّ), a passive participle from the triliteral verb (طوى), on the pattern مفعول.. with a weakening by substitution, its origin being مطووي with ḍamma on the first wāw and sukūn on the second; the second wāw and the yāʾ met in the word, the first of them being quiescent, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and merged with the other yāʾ, and it was said (مطويّ); then the letter before the yāʾ was given kasra for harmony..
(يمينه): interpreted as meaning power and ownership ...

safi-cedvel:14-16.t:
* I'rab:
(الله), the Name of Majesty, is a fronted direct object, accusative; (مخلصا له ديني) is like (مخلصا له الدين) [Note: in verse (11) of this sūra.].
Clause: «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أعبد ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
(15) (الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis, and the imperative in (اعبدوا) is a threat; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object [Note: or an indefinite noun with a descriptive clause, the clause شئتم being its adjective.]; (من دونه) is a ḥāl from the implied returning pronoun; (الذين) is a relative noun, the khabar of إنّ, in the position of nominative; (يوم) is an accusative adverb of time attached to (خسروا); (ألا) is a particle of alerting; (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الخسران, and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.].
And the clause «اعبدوا ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "as for you, worship ..." that is, "you do not worship Allah".
And the clause «شئتم ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّ الخاسرين الذين ...» is in the position of accusative, being the content of the saying.
And the clause «خسروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «ذلك هو الخسران ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
(16) (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ظلل; (من فوقهم) is attached to a ḥāl from ظلل [Note: or attached to the omitted khabar.]; (من النار) is attached to an adjective of ظلل; (من تحتهم) is like من فوقهم; (ظلل) is conjoined to the first with the wāw [Note: it may be a postponed mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (من تحتهم), and the conjunction is then a conjunction of clauses.]; (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ in the position of nominative, and the demonstrative refers to the punishment; (به) is attached to (يخوّف); (يا عباد): its i'rab has already been given [Note: in verse (10) of this sūra.]; (الفاء) is the connector of an omitted conditional apodosis [Note: or redundant, for embellishment.]. The nūn in (اتّقون) is the nūn of protection before the speaker's (yāʾ), which has been omitted to suit the verse ending, and it (the yāʾ) is the direct object.
And the clause «لهم ... ظلل» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive - or gives a reason.
And the clause «ذلك يخوّف به ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «يخوّف ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
And the vocative clause «يا عباد» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive - or the content of the saying of an implied saying.
And the clause «اتّقون» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "if you fear the Fire, then fear Me.." and the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.

* Rhetoric:
Tahwīl (awe-inspiring dread): in His saying, the Exalted: «أَلا ذلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرانُ الْمُبِينُ».
A splendid tahwīl. He made the sentence resumptive and opened it with the particle of alerting, and by that indicated the remoteness of the standing of what is pointed to in evil, and that because of its enormity it is as though perceptible by the senses; He placed the separating pronoun between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, made الخسران definite, brought it in the form فعلان, which is more intensive than فعل, and described it as «المبين» (manifest), which shows the perfection of its terror and its hideousness, and that there is no kind of loss beyond it.

* Benefits:
- The states of the vocative noun annexed to the speaker's yāʾ:
1- If it ends in a weak letter (maqṣūr or manqūṣ), the yāʾ remains with it, with fatḥa, such as:
(يا فتاي، يا محاميّ).
2- If it is an adjective: i.e. (an active participle, its intensive form, or a passive participle), the yāʾ remains with it, quiescent or with fatḥa; you say: (يا سامعي يا سامعي أجبني) (يا معبودي يا معبودي أغثني).
3- If it ends in a sound letter, four options are permitted:
a- Omitting the yāʾ and keeping the kasra before it as an indication of it, as in His saying, the Exalted, in the verse we are dealing with (يا عِبادِ فَاتَّقُونِ). b- Keeping the yāʾ quiescent (يا عبادي). c- Keeping the yāʾ and giving it fatḥa (يا حسرتي على فلان).
d- Turning the kasra before the yāʾ into fatḥa, and the yāʾ into alif, such as: (يا حسرتا). If the muḍāf is أب or أم, the four options above are permitted, and a fifth option is permitted: turning the yāʾ into a tāʾ with fatḥa, such as (يا أبت، يا أمّت), and a sixth option: turning it into a tāʾ with kasra, such as (يا أبت) (يا أمت), and this tāʾ is replaced by hāʾ in pause, so you say: (يا أبه، يا أمّه).
They attached to that (ابن عمي، ابنة عمي، ابن أمي، ابنة أمي), so they permitted in them keeping the yāʾ and omitting it, with kasra or fatḥa on the last letter: (يا بن عمّ، يا بن عمّ), although the speaker's yāʾ here has not had a vocative noun annexed to it, but rather what the vocative noun is annexed to was annexed to it, so its due was to be kept; but they attached it to what came before, indeed their omission of it is more frequent than keeping it.

safi-cedvel:17-18.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is resumptive; (أن) is a maṣdar and accusative-governing particle; (إلى الله) is attached to (أنابوا); (لهم) is attached to a fronted khabar.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يعبدوها) is in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from الطاغوت.
(الفاء) is a conjunction connecting the effect with the cause; (عباد) is a direct object, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on what precedes the speaker's yāʾ, which is omitted because of the reading in connected speech.. and the omitted (الياء) is the muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «الذين اجتنبوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اجتنبوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «يعبدوها ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the literal particle (أن).
And the clause «أنابوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اجتنبوا ...
And the clause «لهم البشرى ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
And the clause «بشرّ عباد ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: "Take heed, and give glad tidings ..."
(18) (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as an adjective of عبادي; (الفاء) is a conjunction; the second (الذين) is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك; (هم) is a separating pronoun [Note: or a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is أولو ... and the nominal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]; (أولو) is the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ أولئك.
And the clause «يستمعون ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «يتّبعون ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause يستمعون.
And the clause «أولئك الذين هداهم ...» has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumptive.
And the clause «هداهم الله ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the third relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «أولئك ... أولو الألباب» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the first clause أولئك ...

* Rhetoric:
Mubālagha (hyperbole): in likening the devil to the Ṭāghūt in His saying, the Exalted: «وَالَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ».
It contains several hyperboles: naming with the maṣdar, as if the very essence of the devil were tyranny (ṭughyān), and the pattern is a pattern of hyperbole, for al-raḥamūt is "the vast mercy", and al-malakūt is "the extended sovereignty",
[Translator's note: the source text breaks off here, after the comma.]

safi-cedvel:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(The hamza) is for interrogation; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ [Note: it is permissible for it to be a relative noun devoid of conditional sense, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "like one who is saved".]; (عليه) is attached to (حقّ); (the hamza) is an emphasis of the first; (الفاء) is the connector of the apodosis; (في النار) is attached to an omitted ṣila of من.
Clause: «من حقّ عليه كلمة ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: or conjoined by the fāʾ to an implied resumptive clause, i.e.: "Is one who disbelieved, then one against whom the word has become due,.."].
And the clause «حقّ عليه كلمة ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من.
And the clause «أنت تنقذ ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition, accompanied by the fāʾ [Note: it is permissible for the apodosis to be omitted, and the mentioned clause to be brought to confirm the content of the preceding clause, the implied apodosis being: "then you will rescue him".].
And the clause «تنقذ ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنت.

* Rhetoric:
Al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya al-makniyya (the representational implicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: «أَفَأَنْتَ تُنْقِذُ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ».
Here the state of him, peace and blessings be upon him, in the intensity of striving to obtain their guidance and in exerting himself in calling them to faith, is likened to the state of one who wants to rescue from the Fire those who are in it. In al-Khafājī's glosses, quoting al-Saʿd (al-Taftāzānī), there is in this verse a metaphor that only the knights of rhetoric recognise, which is the representational implicit metaphor, because He treated what His saying «أفمن» etc. indicates, namely their deserving the punishment while they are in this world, as equivalent to their entering the Fire in the Hereafter, so that it follows that his exerting himself, peace be upon him, in calling them to faith is treated as equivalent to rescuing them from the Fire, which is among the things that go with entering the Fire.
And it was said: the Fire is a majāz for misguidance, by applying the name of the effect (musabbab) to the cause (sabab), and the rescue in place of guidance is of the embellishment (tarshīḥ) of the majāz.

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(لكن) is an inoperative particle of rectification (istidrāk) and has the meaning of iḍrāb (turning away); (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ غرف; (من فوقها) is attached to the fronted khabar of the second mubtadaʾ غرف; (من تحتها) is attached to (تجري), with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "from beneath their courtyards" [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from الأنهار.]; (وعد) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; (لا) is negative.
Clause: «الذين اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «لهم غرف ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
And the clause «من فوقها غرف ...» is in the position of nominative as an adjective of the first غرف.
And the clause «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is in the position of nominative as an adjective of غرف in both places [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from both.].
And the clause «(وعد) الله وعدا» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يخلف الله ...» has no grammatical position; it gives a reason - or is an explanatory resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مبنيّة): the feminine of مبنيّ, a passive participle from the triliteral بنى, and it contains an iʿlāl by substitution: its origin is مبنوي - with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the wāw - the wāw and the yāʾ came together with the first quiescent, so the wāw was turned into yāʾ and assimilated into the second yāʾ, and then the letter before the yāʾ received kasra for harmony.
